summary: The source shows two problems in the binary-operator path. `a, b = pop(), pop()` takes the top of the stack as the left operand, so `SUB`, `LT`, `GT` and `DIV`/`MOD` all see their operands reversed. The `DIV`/`MOD` zero check then looks at the wrong operand, which is why the zero-division test misses. `SWAP` has the same reversed-pop pattern and pushes its values back in the original order, so it does nothing. I'll fix the pop order at the source.
